Dragon-temple — colossal scaled columns frame entrance, carved wing-motifs span architrave, half-collapsed roof reveals interior altar with dragon-skull centerpiece, ancient stone worn smooth by centuries.
Cliff-cut roost — massive cave mouth carved with dragon-face relief, jutting stone platform extends over valley, scored with talon-marks, natural rock columns frame opening darkly.
Mountain-cut tomb — enormous stone doors carved as folded dragon wings, runic glyphs glow faintly along frame, cliff face shaped into snarling dragon head above entrance.
Dragon-shrine — standing stones arranged in circle, each carved with different dragon aspect, central obsidian altar scarred by fire, weathered runes spiral up each monolith surface.
Cathedral-of-bones — massive wyrm ribs arch overhead as structural supports, fused vertebrae form pillars, wing-bones span ceiling like gothic vaults, ancient and sanctified by cult.

Dragon-rider outpost — fortress built into mountain face, wide landing platforms jutting from cliff, scaled battlements, massive chain-mechanisms hang unused, architecture designed for mounted flights.
Scaled-column hall — vast interior corridor lined with pillars carved as dragon necks, heads curve to support ceiling, jeweled eyes glint in shadows, floor polished obsidian.
Vault-of-hoards — stone treasury carved deep into mountain, dragon-claw buttresses support arched ceiling, runic wards etched across sealed door, abandoned treasure chamber looms ominously.

Dragon-cult-monastery — fortified stone complex on mountainside, dragon-wing flying buttresses extend from walls, hooded figures carved in relief worship dragon-deity central statue, crumbling but intact.
Dragon-tooth crenellations — castle wall crowned with massive carved fangs pointing skyward, each battlement shaped as dragon jaw, ancient fortress dominates ridge, silhouetted against stormy sky.
Colonnade-of-claws — processional way lined with pillars carved as dragon legs, stone talons grip earth, each column unique dragon species, path leads to distant temple ruins.

Dragon-fortified-keep — tower fortress with dragon-skull gatehouse, scaled walls rise steeply, wing-shaped parapets extend from corners, built to withstand and house dragons simultaneously, partially ruined.
Dragon-tomb-marker-field — valley floor dotted with stone monuments carved as coiled dragons, each marking ancient wyrm burial site, moss-covered sentinels stretch toward misty mountains beyond.
Aerie — high mountain platform carved from living rock, dragon-perch stones jut upward, open to sky, wind-worn stairs spiral down cliff face, abandoned roost overlooks vast landscape.

Dragon-cathedral — towering gothic structure with dragon-eye rose windows, flying buttresses shaped as folded wings, scale-textured stone walls, massive doors carved with dragon history panels, majestic ruin.

Dragon-fire altar — circular stone platform carved with flame motifs, central brazier shaped as dragon maw, surrounding pillars topped with dragon-head capitals breathe eternal flame, mountaintop temple.

Wyrm-skeleton gatehouse — colossal dragon skull forms entrance arch, vertebrae extend as tunnel walls, ribcage supports ceiling above passage, petrified remains integrated into fortress architecture permanently.
Dragon-glyph obelisk — towering stone spire carved with spiraling runic dragon script, weathered but readable, stands alone in wasteland, monument to ancient dragon-pact, lightning-scarred peak.
Scaled-dome sanctuary — domed building with roof carved as overlapping dragon scales, metallic sheen despite stone construction, dragon-claw finial tops structure, circular temple in clearing.

Dragon-watch tower — slender fortress spire with dragon-head gargoyles at corners, observation platform designed for rider-mount pairs, claw-marked stone, defensive outpost overlooking border valleys below.
Petrified-flame colonnade — row of columns carved as frozen dragonfire, orange-red veined stone, organic flame-like curves support arched roof, processional path through ancient dragon-worship site.
Dragon-throne dais — raised platform carved from single stone block, dragon-claw armrests, scaled backrest rises high, empty seat in ruined throne room, built for dragon-lord or rider-king.
Wing-vault chapel — small shrine with ceiling carved as spread dragon wings meeting at peak, feather-scale details, dragon-eye window above altar casts colored light, hillside pilgrimage site.
Dragon-horn spires — twin towers carved spiraling upward like dragon horns, linked by bridge carved as spine, fortress crown overlooks kingdom, ancient construction defies time weathering.

Claw-carved buttresses — fortress exterior reinforced by massive stone supports carved as dragon legs grasping walls, talons dig into foundation, architectural defense and dragon-homage combined, formidable stronghold.
